Fidelity notes: the adopted text says 'contextual factors' (rendered here as 'context/contextual factors'); §120.21(d)(1)(B) also specifies 'when heard during formal and informal classroom interactions' and response modalities, trimmed in the short summary. 2026-10-28 expansion: added 9 §120.20 (K–3) listening/speaking/reading codes and 9 more §120.21 (4–12) codes; every added code was compared word-for-word between TEA ch120b.pdf (currently-in-effect) and Cornell LII §§120.20/120.21 — the full (d) student-expectation text of both sections matches (only PDF line-break hyphenation differs). standards.summary: Use high-frequency words, contextual factors, cognates, and Greek and Latin prefixes, suffixes, and roots to comprehend content-area vocabulary in text.
Decode words using sound-letter relationships and identify syllable patterns, cognates, affixes, roots, or base words.
Use context or word analysis — such as cognates and Greek and Latin prefixes, suffixes, and roots — to comprehend content-specific vocabulary heard during classroom interactions.
Speak using content-area vocabulary during classroom interactions to demonstrate acquisition of new and high-frequency words.
Use high-frequency words, cognates, and content-area vocabulary to comprehend written classroom materials.
Restate, ask questions about, or respond to information during formal and informal classroom interactions.
Speak using an appropriate register (formal or informal) to convey a message during classroom interactions.
Respond with accuracy to oral directions, instructions, and requests.
Show understanding of content-area vocabulary heard during formal and informal classroom interactions by responding with gestures or images, orally, or in writing.
Follow oral directions with accuracy.
Use context to understand descriptive language, multiple-meaning words, register, or figurative language such as idioms heard during classroom interactions.
Show listening comprehension of information presented orally by recalling, retelling, responding, or asking for clarification or more details.
Speak using content-area vocabulary during formal and informal classroom interactions to show acquisition of new and high-frequency words.
Speak using an appropriate register to convey a message during formal and informal classroom interactions with accuracy and fluency.
Narrate, describe, explain information, or persuade orally with increasing specificity and detail during classroom interactions.
Restate, ask questions about, or respond to information during formal and informal classroom interactions.
Derive meaning from and show comprehension of content-area texts using visual, contextual, and linguistic supports.
Use context to understand descriptive language, multiple-meaning words, register, and figurative language such as idioms heard during classroom interactions.
Show listening comprehension of information presented orally by restating, responding, paraphrasing, summarizing, or asking for clarification or more details.
Pronounce words — including high-frequency words, cognates, and increasingly complex syllable types — with accuracy.
Speak using a variety of language and grammatical structures, sentence lengths and types, and transition words.
Narrate, describe, explain, justify, discuss, elaborate, or evaluate orally with increasing specificity and detail in academic contexts.
Use context to understand figurative language such as idioms, descriptive language, and multiple-meaning words in a variety of texts.
Derive meaning from and show comprehension of content-area texts using visual, contextual, and linguistic supports.
Write content-area texts using a variety of sentence lengths and types and transition words.
Write to narrate, describe, explain, respond, or justify with supporting details and evidence, using content, style, register, and conventions suited to purpose and audience.
